text:
**Recommendation: A "Mobile-First, Offline-First" System Using Open-Source Tools + Low-Cost Android Tablets**  

Given the constraints (intermittent power, no internet, low digital literacy, 30 staff, PHP 400,000 budget, 18-month horizon), the best approach is **not** to build a custom web app or buy expensive cloud software. Instead, use **offline-capable, open-source tools** that run on cheap Android tablets, with a simple paper-to-digital workflow.

---

### 1. Core Tools & Hardware

| Item | Tool / Spec | Purpose | Cost (PHP) |
|------|-------------|---------|------------|
| **Data collection & case management** | **KoboToolbox** (free, open-source) – install on local server or use their free tier, but **use the Android app "KoboCollect"** which works fully offline. | Field staff fill forms (client intake, health visits, follow-ups) on tablets. Data syncs when internet is available. | PHP 0 (software) |
| **Offline server (for data storage & reporting)** | **Raspberry Pi 4 (4GB)** + external SSD + **KoboToolbox Server** (self-hosted) OR **ODK Central** (open-source). | Acts as the "central brain" in the main office. Staff sync tablets to this via Wi-Fi (even a portable hotspot) when they return to base. | PHP 15,000 (Pi + SSD + case) |
| **Tablets (10 units)** | **Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 Lite (32GB)** – durable, long battery, cheap. | 10 field staff use these; the rest share or use paper backups. | PHP 10,000 × 10 = PHP 100,000 |
| **Portable power banks** | Anker 20,000mAh (2 per tablet team) | For intermittent electricity. | PHP 1,500 × 20 = PHP 30,000 |
| **Portable Wi-Fi hotspot** | Globe/Smart prepaid pocket Wi-Fi (2 units) | For syncing data at office or field when signal exists. | PHP 3,000 × 2 = PHP 6,000 |
| **Training & change management** | Hire a local IT trainer for 5 days (offline, hands-on) | Teach staff to use KoboCollect, scan QR codes, and follow simple data entry rules. | PHP 40,000 |
| **Printing & QR codes** | Print client ID cards with QR codes (using free QR generator) | Each client gets a unique ID – staff scan instead of typing names. | PHP 5,000 |
| **Backup & maintenance** | External hard drive (2TB) + spare tablet screen protector/cases | Weekly manual backup from Pi to drive. | PHP 8,000 |
| **Contingency (10%)** | – | For broken tablets, extra cables, unexpected costs. | PHP 40,000 |
| **Total** | | | **PHP 244,000** |

**Remaining budget: PHP 156,000** – keep as a **sustainability reserve** (see below).

---

### 2. How the System Works (Step-by-Step)

1. **Field staff** carry a tablet with **KoboCollect** app. They open the app, see a simple form (in Filipino/English) with dropdowns, checkboxes, and photo capture. No typing required – mostly tapping.
2. **Client identification** – each client gets a printed card with a QR code. Staff scan the QR to auto-fill client name/ID.
3. **Offline data entry** – all data is stored locally on the tablet (SQLite database). No internet needed.
4. **Sync when possible** – when staff return to the office or find a signal, they press "Sync" – data uploads to the **Raspberry Pi server** (via Wi-Fi hotspot or office router).
5. **Office staff** use a simple web dashboard (KoboToolbox) on a laptop to view reports, export Excel, and track follow-ups.
6. **Paper backup** – for the first 3 months, staff also keep a paper logbook as a fallback, then phase it out.

---

### 3. What Happens When Donor Funding Ends (After 18 Months)

**The system does NOT die.** Here’s why:

- **No recurring software fees** – KoboToolbox and ODK Central are open-source. The Raspberry Pi server is owned outright.
- **Hardware lasts 3–5 years** – tablets, power banks, and Pi will still function.
- **Staff skills remain** – after 18 months, staff will be comfortable with the tools. Training is a one-time cost.
- **Maintenance costs are minimal** – only replacement of broken tablets (PHP 10k each) or a new Pi (PHP 15k) every few years. This can be covered by the **PHP 156,000 reserve** you keep unspent.
- **If internet improves** – you can later migrate to a free cloud server (e.g., KoboToolbox’s free tier for NGOs) without changing the app.

**Risk mitigation:**  
- Keep the **PHP 156,000** in a separate bank account as a "tech maintenance fund."  
- After 12 months, train 2 "super-users" on the staff to troubleshoot basic issues.  
- If the organization grows, they can apply for small grants or use local government health funds to replace hardware.

---

### 4. Why This Beats Alternatives

- **Cloud SaaS (e.g., Salesforce, mHealth apps)** – requires internet, monthly fees, and high digital literacy – fails your constraints.
- **Building a custom app** – costs PHP 400k+ just for development, and you’d still need hardware and training.
- **Laptops** – too heavy, fragile, and power-hungry for field work.

**Final answer:** Use **KoboCollect + Raspberry Pi server + Android tablets** – total cost **PHP 244,000**, leaving **PHP 156,000** as a sustainability buffer. The system is fully owned, offline-first, and will continue functioning after donor funding ends, with minimal ongoing costs.
